ulysses.title: Library & sheets
ulysses.summary: Everything is a sheet in a three-pane library (groups, sheet list, editor). A line that starts with ? runs an agent and the answer is written into the same sheet as plain prose, so a chat and a note are the same object. Branches attach to marked passages, glued sheets form a manuscript whose headings are the outline, and [[links]] plus keywords populate a References view.

variants.label: Prose, margin branches
variants.summary: Questions and answers read as one continuous text with markup in the margin; branches are numbered margin notes beside the marked passage.

variants.label: Chat bubbles
variants.summary: Questions render as right-aligned bubbles under a sheet title; answers stay plain prose; everything else matches A.

variants.label: Branches as attachments
variants.summary: Branches leave the margin and are listed as attached sheets in the open attachments panel; passages keep a numbered marker.

variants.label: Two panes
variants.summary: The library collapses into a group menu above the sheet list and the attachments panel stays open, which leaves more room on small screens.

variants.label: Outline first
variants.summary: Opens on the Chapter 3 manuscript in Outline view; chats are reached from outline rows rather than from the sheet list.

macos.title: Mac system app
macos.influence: Apple macOS system app idioms (HIG; Finder, Mail, Messages, Freeform, System Settings)
macos.summary: Session becomes a standard Mac document app: a glass sidebar of folders, one toolbar view switch (Page, Outline, Columns, Map) over the same library, and an inspector (⌥⌘I) that holds a chat's branches and links. Chats read like Messages, notes are collapsible outlines with [[links]], and the first window offers one field — ask a question — with the agent check done in the background.

variants.label: Page + inspector
variants.summary: Opens on a chat in Page view with a Mail-style item list and an inspector holding Info, Branches and Links.

variants.label: Column browser
variants.summary: Opens in Columns view: folders → items → branches and bullets → Quick Look preview, replacing the column strip.

variants.label: Outline list
variants.summary: Opens in Outline view: one disclosure-triangle list of folders, chats, branches and note bullets; Space opens Quick Look.

variants.label: Popover branches
variants.summary: No inspector by default; numbered passage markers open branches in popovers, with an opaque, denser sidebar.

variants.label: Map canvas
variants.summary: Opens on a canvas map of chats, notes, highlights and links grouped by folder; the inspector follows the selected card.

notes.title: Notes with Ask
notes.summary: Session becomes a three-pane notes app: folders, a dated note list, and a note whose first line is its title. Any note can run a model inline (⌘J); answers stay in the note as editable text, and selecting a passage branches it into a linked sub-note. Outline and Link Map are two more views of the same notes, so there is one object to learn.

variants.label: Inline chats
variants.summary: Chats run as blocks inside the note; branches nest as sub-notes in the list; Linked Notes sits at the bottom of each note.

variants.label: Chat side panel
variants.summary: The note holds only the answer text; the conversation (questions, run status, follow-up box) lives in a panel beside it.

variants.label: Replies section
variants.summary: Branches do not appear in the note list; they are numbered on the passage and listed in a Replies section at the end of the note.

variants.label: Gallery home
variants.summary: Folders open in gallery view with run status on each thumbnail; Quick Note is the primary capture path.

variants.label: Link inspector
variants.summary: A right-hand inspector shows a mini link map, backlinks and tags for the open note; the tag browser shows counts.

obsidian.title: Vault of linked notes
obsidian.summary: Everything is a Markdown note in a local vault: a chat is a note whose body holds Ask blocks, a branch is a new note linked to the highlighted passage it came from, and backlinks, the outline pane and the graph are computed from those links. Every empty tab and the first-run screen lead with one Ask box, and agent sign-in never blocks writing or queueing.

variants.label: Asks as callouts
variants.summary: Chats are notes; each question and answer renders as a foldable callout, with backlinks over a local graph in the right sidebar.

variants.label: Chat in sidebar
variants.summary: Composing moves to a right-sidebar Chat pane bound to the open note; answers are inserted into notes as callouts on request.

variants.label: Transcript blocks
variants.summary: Same structure as A, but asks render as a plain transcript (labelled question, ruled answer) instead of tinted callouts.

variants.label: Graph split pane
variants.summary: The global graph opens beside the note in a split pane and follows the active note; the right sidebar starts closed.

variants.label: Starter vault
variants.summary: First launch shows an ask-first welcome screen; the sample vault opens on a Start here note with a checklist tracked in the sidebar.

notion.title: Pages & blocks
notion.summary: Everything is a page made of blocks: a chat is a page whose blocks are questions and answers, a note is a page you write, and a branch is a sub-chat nested under the passage it came from. One sidebar tree, @-links with backlinks, a Questions database (table/board/list/gallery) and a link map replace folders, feeds and three save gestures. First run opens a Getting started page with a single Ask box; agent setup is a non-blocking checklist item.

variants.label: Chat pages
variants.summary: Chats are pages in the tree; branches are sub-chat pages listed under the passage they came from; first run lands on Getting started.

variants.label: Questions database
variants.summary: Every chat is a row in a Questions database with Status, Agent and Model properties; the database is the landing view and chat pages show their properties.

variants.label: Branches as toggles
variants.summary: Sub-chats render inline as toggle blocks under the passage instead of separate pages, so one investigation reads as one page.

variants.label: Side peek
variants.summary: Outline-first: the Chapter 3 note is the landing page and chats open in a side peek beside it, keeping the note in view.

variants.label: Inline AI blocks
variants.summary: Questions are asked from an inline AI block at the end of any page; the chat composer is a block in the page flow rather than a docked bar.

inbox.title: Research inbox
inbox.influence: Front / Missive / Superhuman / Hey (shared email inbox apps)
inbox.summary: Every question is a Conversation that runs in the background and lands in an Inbox as “Ready to read”; queued and running ones sit in Waiting. Follow-ups are Ask replies, your own writing is a Note (the internal-comment idiom), and a passage can start a Fork. Tags, [[links]], backlinks and a Knowledge view with outline and graph replace folders, stars, bookmarks and the feed, so the first screen has one action: ask.

variants.label: Triage inbox
variants.summary: Three panes: mailboxes, one list per mailbox (Inbox, Waiting, Done), conversation, and a details sidebar with links and forks.

variants.label: Split inbox
variants.summary: The Inbox list is split into Ready to read, Waiting and Read sections, so running work is visible without switching mailboxes.

variants.label: Compose-first home
variants.summary: Inbox opens on a New conversation pane with suggestions from your notes, and the list has an inline quick-ask box.

variants.label: Notes in sidebar
variants.summary: No separate Knowledge view: notes and the outline open in a sidebar tab beside the conversation; the graph opens as an overlay.

variants.label: Compact, keyboard
variants.summary: Single-line rows, details sidebar closed by default, and a persistent shortcut bar for j/k, e, s, r, n, f triage.

tana.title: Everything is a node
tana.influence: Tana (with nods to Roam Research, Logseq, Workflowy)
tana.summary: Chats and notes live in one outline. A question is a node tagged #question: ⌘↵ runs it, the answer arrives as child nodes, follow-ups are child questions, and a selected passage becomes a #claim node that can be referenced anywhere. Home is today's page with one input line (⌘↵ asks, ↵ saves a note), so there is one first action and one place where everything lands.

variants.label: Prose answers
variants.summary: Answers arrive as one node per paragraph, tag fields render inline, and references are listed at the bottom of each page.

variants.label: Claim answers
variants.summary: The same answer is split into #claim nodes grouped under topic nodes, each with its source shown beside it.

variants.label: Fields as table
variants.summary: Tag fields render as a bordered field table, and live searches inside the outline render as tables.

variants.label: Workspace home
variants.summary: Home is the workspace outline instead of today's page, and the sidebar shows the outline tree instead of pins.

variants.label: References panel
variants.summary: A persistent side panel shows references and a local map for the current node, and bullets carry reference counts.

linear.title: Questions & Notes
linear.summary: Every investigation is a Question with one visible status (Queued, Running, Ready, Reviewed) and an agent as its assignee; sub-questions replace branches, Notes are outline documents, and Links are typed connections you can list or graph. One dense, keyboard-first list replaces the mixed chat-and-feed Home, so the first action is always the same: press C and ask.

variants.label: List + document
variants.summary: Home is a status-grouped list; a question opens as a document with sub-questions and an activity log below the answer.

variants.label: Board home
variants.summary: Home is a status board (Queued, Running, Ready, Reviewed) instead of a grouped list; the question page is unchanged.

variants.label: Conversation page
variants.summary: The question page is chat-centric: question, answers, follow-ups and run events read as one timeline, with sub-questions inline as events.

variants.label: Peek split
variants.summary: Clicking a row opens a docked preview beside the list (triage-style); Enter or double-click opens the full page.

variants.label: Links as graph
variants.summary: Links render as a graph: the question sidebar shows a local mini-graph, and the Links view opens on the workspace graph.

ulysses.title: Library & sheets
ulysses.summary: Everything is a sheet in a three-pane library (groups, sheet list, editor). The question line docked under every sheet runs an agent and writes the answer into that sheet as prose, so a chat and a note are the same object. Any passage can be marked, branched, or filed under a heading of the Chapter 3 outline; glued sheets form the outline, and [[links]] plus keywords build the Links map.

variants.label: Margin branches
variants.summary: Answers read as continuous prose with markup in the margin; branches are numbered notes in a fixed right margin, level with their passage.

variants.label: Inline branches
variants.summary: Branches sit as indented strips directly under the paragraph they came from and show the full branch answer in place; the text column stays centered.

variants.label: Branches as attachments
variants.summary: Branches are listed as attached sheets in the attachments panel, which opens by default; passages keep a numbered marker.

variants.label: Two panes
variants.summary: The library folds into a group menu above the sheet list and the attachments panel stays open, for smaller screens.

variants.label: Outline first
variants.summary: Opens on the Chapter 3 manuscript in Outline view, with File and Link actions on every row; chats are reached from outline rows.

changes: Docked the question line to the bottom of the editor; in round 1 it sat after the last answer and was off-screen on long sheets.
Added File in… to passage actions and answer footers: it adds a linked bullet under a chosen heading of the Chapter 3 outline. Round 1 could only glue whole sheets or copy to Drafts.
Added [[ autocomplete in the question line and a Link… action on outline rows; round 1 had no way to create a link.
Paragraph gutter button (¶) opens Mark / Ask / Branch / File without selecting text; round 1 relied on selection.
Branches are numbered in reading order and branches from a whole answer sit at its end; round 1 showed 2 above 1.
Replaced the Chat bubbles variant with Inline branches; bubbles broke the typographic idiom and changed nothing about organizing.
First run: library shows only Inbox, missing agents show a copyable command and re-check automatically; the main workspace gains a dismissible ‘how sheets work’ tip and a visible Search field.
Fixed controls that did nothing: Retry with another model now picks a model, New group creates a group, Glue is disabled where it does not apply.
decisions: Does the ? / ¶ glyph make the difference between asking and writing clear without reading the tip?
Margin notes (A), inline strips (B) or attachments (C): which lets people find a branch again after a day?
Is File in… (linked bullet) understood as different from Glue (whole sheet joins the manuscript)?
Do people use the Links map, or only the References lists under it?

macos.title: Mac system app
macos.influence: Apple macOS system app idioms (HIG; Finder, Mail, Messages, Freeform, System Settings, TipKit)
macos.summary: Session as a standard Mac document app: a glass sidebar of folders, an always-visible “Ask a question” field at the top of the item list, and one toolbar switch (Page, Outline, Columns, Map) over the same library. Chats read like Messages, notes are outlines with [[links]], and three short tips walk a new user from first question to branch to links; agents are detected in the background and never block writing notes.

variants.label: Page + inspector
variants.summary: Mail-style list with a docked Ask field, the chat page, and an inspector (⌥⌘I) with Info, Branches and Links; first-run tips are shown.

variants.label: Column browser
variants.summary: Opens in Columns view: folders → items → branches and bullets → a Quick Look preview with the passage actions, replacing the column strip.

variants.label: Outline list
variants.summary: Opens in Outline view: one disclosure-triangle list of folders, chats, branches and note bullets; Space opens Quick Look, drag reorders or files.

variants.label: Messages threads
variants.summary: Answers sit in incoming bubbles and branches appear as reply threads under the answer, Messages-style; no inspector by default.

variants.label: Map canvas
variants.summary: Opens on a Freeform-style map of chats, notes, highlights and links grouped by folder; the inspector follows the selected card.

changes: Added a docked “Ask a question” field above every item list; in round 1 the only way to start a chat was an unlabeled toolbar icon
Added three TipKit-style tips (ask → branch → links) with Next and dismiss; round 1 had no guidance outside the empty Personal workspace
Branch composer now opens as a popover on the passage in every variant; in round 1 it opened in the inspector, far from the selected text
Add to Note lists the outline's sections and the confirmation has a Show button that opens the note at the new bullet; round 1 appended silently to the end
Added Link to… in the Links inspector, so any two chats or notes can be linked without writing a note; links appear in both items and on the map
First-run workspace now shows only the welcome page (no empty list or empty inspector) and checks agents live, re-checking when the window becomes active
Return sends in every composer (⌥↩ new line, ⇧⌘↩ branch), matching Messages; round 1 required ⌘↩ and the hint was easy to miss

Replaced the weak “Popover branches” variant with “Messages threads”; fixed narrow-width navigation (no way back to the list), flat-list bolding, “1 items”, and passage keys ignored while the search field had focus
decisions: Is the docked Ask field in the list pane found before the toolbar compose button, and does Return-to-send surprise people writing long questions?
Do people understand that Page, Outline, Columns and Map show the same items, or do they expect four separate places?
Branch as inspector cards (a) or as reply threads under the answer (d): which do first-time users find and reopen faster?
Is “Link to…” in the inspector used, or do people only link by typing [[ in notes?
Do three sequential tips help, or are they dismissed unread?

notes.title: Notes with Ask
notes.summary: Session becomes a three-pane notes app: folders, a dated note list, and a note whose first line is its title. It opens on a pinned Start Here note with one ask box; any note can run a model inline (⌘J), and every answer paragraph has a margin button to ask about it, branch it into a sub-note, or add it to another note. Outline and Link Map are two more views of the same notes, so there is one object to learn.

variants.label: Inline chats
variants.summary: Chats run as blocks inside the note; branches nest as sub-notes in the list; Linked Notes sits at the bottom of each note.

variants.label: Chat side panel
variants.summary: The note holds only the answer text; questions, run status and the follow-up box live in a panel beside it.

variants.label: Replies section
variants.summary: Branches stay out of the note list; they are numbered on the passage and listed in a Replies section at the end of the note.

variants.label: Ask-first notes
variants.summary: The compose button makes a chat and every new note opens with the ask line under the title; writing plain text is one Escape away.

variants.label: Link inspector
variants.summary: A right-hand inspector shows a mini link map, backlinks, sub-notes and tags for the open note; the tag browser shows counts.

changes: Opens on a pinned Start Here note with one ask box and a five-step checklist that ticks itself off; round 1 opened on a finished answer with no starting point.
Every answer paragraph has a margin ↳ button (Ask, Ask in New Note, Highlight, Add to Note); in round 1 branching existed only on text selection (issue S-07).
Add to Note… files a passage as a linked bullet into a chosen note and section; round 1 could not file part of an answer, and its Link button only showed a toast.
Split New Note (⌘N) from New Chat (⇧⌘N) and kept ⌘J as Ask in This Note; in round 1 ⌘J was the only entry and appended to whichever note was open.
Links made with >> or from a selection are saved and update Linked Notes, the outline and the Link Map; opening a search result highlights the match in the note.
Format, Table, Lock, Share and New Folder now act (Lock = never sent to a model); in round 1 five toolbar buttons did nothing.
Replaced Gallery home (thumbnail text was unreadable) with Ask-first notes; Quick Note moved from ⌃⌘Q, which is the macOS Lock Screen shortcut, to fn Q.
Model setup re-checks by itself after sign-in and starts the queued chat (issue S-08); round 1 needed a manual Check Again.
decisions: Should a new note start as a chat (d) or as plain text with ⌘J to ask (a)?
Inline chat blocks (a) or a conversation panel (b): which makes it clearer what is model output and what is your own writing?
Do sub-notes belong in the note list (a) or only as Replies inside the parent note (c)?
Is the margin ↳ button found without the Start Here checklist pointing at it?
Is “Lock: never sent to a model” understood without explanation?

obsidian.title: Vault of linked notes
obsidian.summary: Everything is a Markdown note in a local vault: a chat is a note whose body holds Ask blocks, a branch is a new note linked to the passage it came from, and filing a passage puts a linked bullet under a chosen outline heading. The Ask box is pinned to the bottom of every note and every empty tab, each paragraph has a margin button for branch, ask and file, and agent sign-in never blocks writing or queueing.

variants.label: Asks as callouts
variants.summary: Chats are notes; each question and answer is a foldable callout, with backlinks over a local graph in the right sidebar.

variants.label: Chat in sidebar
variants.summary: Composing moves to a right-sidebar Chat pane bound to the open note; answers enter notes only when inserted or filed.

variants.label: Outline beside chat
variants.summary: The vault opens with the Chapter 3 outline and the chat side by side; drag a paragraph's margin handle onto a bullet to file it.

variants.label: Graph split pane
variants.summary: The global graph sits beside the note in a split pane and follows the active note; the right sidebar starts closed.

variants.label: Starter vault
variants.summary: First launch shows an ask-first welcome screen; the sample vault opens on a Start here note with a tracked checklist.

changes: Added a branch button in the left margin of every paragraph with Branch, Ask, File and Copy link; in round 1 these appeared only after selecting text.
File to note now asks for a section and inserts a linked bullet under it; round 1 could only append an embed after the outline.
Pinned the Ask box to the bottom of each note; in round 1 it sat after the last answer, about 1,400 px below the fold.
Getting started card in every variant's sidebar and in empty vaults; round 1 explained the app only in variant E.
Replaced the cosmetic Transcript variant with Outline beside chat, where paragraphs drag from an answer onto outline bullets.
Outline bullets keep typed edits, autocomplete [[links]] and have a Link to… menu; round 1 lost edits on re-render.
Graph labels skip overlaps; notes take aliases, so search or ⌘O for “recap” finds the CAISO summary.
Mobile bottom toolbar, Tab-trapped dialogs, 4.5:1 placeholder text, and menus that say why an item is disabled.
decisions: Does “a chat is a note” hold up when a note mixes writing and asks, or do people look for a separate chat list?
Which do first-time users find first: the margin button or the selection popover?
Should filing insert a linked bullet (current) or transclude the passage inline?
Is “Answer in: This note / New note” enough to predict where an answer is saved?
Does today’s daily note work as Home, or do people want a vault-wide activity list?

notion.title: Pages & blocks
notion.summary: Everything is a page made of blocks: a chat is a page whose blocks are questions and answers, a note is a page you write, and a branch is a sub-chat attached to the passage it came from. Answers file into an outline section as synced bullets that link back, any bullet takes @-links, and backlinks, a local graph and a Map show how pages relate. An empty workspace opens on one Getting started page whose first block is the Ask box; agent status is an inline block, never a gate.

variants.label: Chat pages
variants.summary: Sub-chats are pages listed under the passage they came from and nested in the sidebar; first run lands on Getting started.

variants.label: Home + database
variants.summary: Home is the landing page: the Ask box sits above a linked Questions database (table or board), and chat pages show Status, Agent and Model as properties.

variants.label: Branches as toggles
variants.summary: Sub-chats render inline as toggle blocks under the passage instead of separate pages, so one investigation reads as one page.

variants.label: Side peek
variants.summary: Outline-first: the Chapter 3 note is the landing page and chats open in a side peek beside it, keeping the note in view.

variants.label: Branches in margin
variants.summary: Anchored sub-chats run as margin threads beside their highlight, like comments, with a reply box; the page shifts left to make room.

changes: Added a branch button (⑂) in every answer paragraph's gutter and a Branch button under each answer; in round 1 branching was found only by selecting text (S-07).
Add to page… now files into a chosen outline section as a synced bullet that links back to the chat; in round 1 it appended a block below the outline where it was not visible.
Outline bullets are editable and @ / [[ opens a filtered page picker in any bullet; in round 1 only the empty last line accepted links.
The Personal workspace is actually empty: its own Getting started, no Thesis pages in Search, Map, Highlights or Home; round 1 leaked Thesis content into it.
Getting started steps have Show me buttons that open the right page and point at the control; agent setup is an inline status block with Check again (S-04, S-08).
Links panel gains a local graph and Map gains a focus mode from Show on map; round 1 showed only lists and an unfocused full map.
Replaced the database-landing variant with Home + linked database so the Ask box stays first, and replaced inline AI blocks with margin threads, a stronger alternative for anchored branches.
Placeholder contrast raised to 4.5:1, dialogs trap Tab, the selection toolbar collapses to icons at narrow widths, and a ? button explains the five nouns (S-14, S-17).
decisions: Sub-chat as a page (a), a toggle (c), or a margin thread (e): which do first-time users follow back to its passage most reliably?
Does the ⑂ gutter button get found without the Getting started hint, or is the Branch button under the answer what people use?
Is filing an answer as a synced outline bullet understood as a live copy, or do users expect a one-time paste?
Should the landing view be Getting started (a), Home with the Questions database (b) or the outline (d) once the workspace has content?
Are Page and Chat enough as top-level words, or do people still look for folders?

inbox.title: Research inbox
inbox.influence: Front / Missive / Superhuman / Hey (shared email inbox apps)
inbox.summary: Every question is a Conversation that runs in the background and lands in an Inbox as “Ready to read”; queued and running ones sit in Waiting. Follow-ups are Ask replies, your own writing is a Note (the internal-comment idiom), and a passage can start a Fork. Tags, [[links]], backlinks and a Knowledge view with outline and graph replace folders, stars, bookmarks and the feed, so the first screen has one action: ask.

variants.label: Triage inbox
variants.summary: Three panes: mailboxes, one list per mailbox (Inbox, Waiting, Done), conversation, and a details sidebar with links and forks.

variants.label: Split inbox
variants.summary: The Inbox list is split into Ready to read, Waiting and Read sections, so running work is visible without switching mailboxes.

variants.label: Compose-first home
variants.summary: Inbox opens on a New conversation pane with suggestions from your notes, and the list has an inline quick-ask box.

variants.label: Notes in sidebar
variants.summary: No separate Knowledge view: notes and the outline open in a sidebar tab beside the conversation; the graph opens as an overlay.

variants.label: Margin threads
variants.summary: Forks and highlights anchored to a passage sit in a margin column beside the answer, joined to the passage; the details sidebar starts closed.

changes: Added a Get started checklist with coach marks to the sidebar; in round 1 a new user saw a populated inbox and nothing said what to do first.
Typing [[ in an outline item, a note or a question now opens link suggestions, and Link (L) links any two items; round 1 required typing exact titles.
Search matches answer text and summaries and shows the matching snippet; in round 1 '11.8 TWh' did not find the CAISO conversation.

The sidebar map now shows only the open item and its direct links, with labels; round 1 drew the whole graph too small to read. The graph view adds a This note / Whole workspace switch and a Tags toggle.
Enter sends and Shift-Enter adds a line in every composer, and Stop is also in the composer; round 1 mixed Enter and Cmd-Enter, and the header kept showing Running after a stop.
First run explains the run lifecycle (Ask, Waiting, Inbox, Fork or file, Knowledge), hides the empty details sidebar and uses per-workspace tags; round 1 showed the Thesis tags in an empty workspace.
Replaced the Compact variant with Margin threads, which tests where forks appear; Compact only changed row density.
Agent setup steps, New tag, New workspace and source links now work; in round 1 they only showed a toast.
decisions: Is Note clear for both an outline document and a comment inside a conversation, or do these need two words?
Do first-time users expect a finished, read conversation to stay in the Inbox until marked Done, as in email?
Fork cards under the answer (a) or in the margin beside the passage (e): which do people find without the checklist?
Is a separate Knowledge view needed, or is the sidebar Notes tab (d) enough for outlining?
Do tags cover what people used folders, stars and bookmarks for?

tana.title: Everything is a node
tana.influence: Tana (with nods to Roam Research, Logseq, Workflowy)
tana.summary: Chats and notes live in one outline. A question is a node tagged #question: ⌘↵ runs it, the answer arrives as child nodes, follow-ups are child questions, and any passage can be added to another node as a reference with one key (R). Every page ends in the same input line (⌘↵ asks, ↵ adds a note), and the first run states what Session does and which agent is ready.

variants.label: Prose answers
variants.summary: Answers arrive as one node per paragraph; paragraph actions and follow-up markers sit in the right margin; references are listed at the bottom of each page.

variants.label: Claim answers
variants.summary: The same answer is split into #claim nodes grouped under topic nodes, each with its source beside it, so a claim can be added to the outline directly.

variants.label: Capture bar
variants.summary: The input line is pinned to the bottom of the window on every page and names the node it adds to, as in a chat app.

variants.label: Workspace home
variants.summary: Home is the workspace outline instead of today's page, and the sidebar shows the outline tree instead of pins.

variants.label: References panel
variants.summary: A persistent side panel shows references and a local map for the current node, and bullets carry reference counts.

changes: The input line is now the last line of every page (pinned to the window in C); in round 1 it was at the top of daily pages and at the bottom elsewhere (S-10).

Paragraph actions moved into the right margin, and a passage with follow-ups shows a persistent '↳ 1 follow-up' marker; in round 1 hover buttons covered the text and anchored follow-ups were invisible at the passage (S-07).
Added 'Add to…' (R on a selection, or in the margin) that puts a reference to a passage or node into any outline node; round 1 had no direct way to file part of an answer into Chapter 3.
Search matches Summary fields and retired terms ('recap', 'highlight', 'bookmark', 'branch') and says what replaced them; in round 1 'recap' found nothing.
First run states what Session does, shows the detected agent as Ready, and keeps a 0/4 checklist above the focused input; round 1 relied on a bullet list.
Today's live search no longer repeats items already on the page, map labels no longer overlap, and placeholder text meets 4.5:1 (S-17).
Replaced the cosmetic 'Fields as table' variant with 'Capture bar'; disabled menu items show their reason inline (S-16) and the Agents panel re-checks automatically (S-08).
decisions: Does an answer laid out as outline nodes read as a chat transcript, or do first-time users expect message bubbles?
Which input do people find without help: the last line of the page (A) or the pinned capture bar (C)?
Is the difference between File in (move a question) and Add to (reference anything) clear, or should it be one gesture?
Prose paragraphs (A) or claim nodes (B) as the default answer shape?
Do ringed reference bullets communicate 'the same node, shown here'?

linear.title: Questions & Notes
linear.summary: Every investigation is a Question with one visible status (Queued, Running, Ready, Reviewed) and an agent as its assignee; sub-questions replace branches, Notes are outline documents, and Links are typed connections listed on both items and drawn as a graph grouped by project. One keyboard-first list replaces the mixed chat-and-feed Home, so the first action is always the same: press C and ask; filing an answer into the outline is one menu away from any passage.

variants.label: List + document
variants.summary: Home is a status-grouped list; a question opens as a document with sub-questions and an activity log below the answer.

variants.label: Project home
variants.summary: Opens on the project outline (sections as milestones, linked questions nested under each line) and lists projects first in the sidebar; the question list is one level down.

variants.label: Conversation page
variants.summary: The question page is chat-centric: question, answers, follow-ups and run events read as one timeline, with sub-questions inline as events.

variants.label: Peek split
variants.summary: Clicking a row opens a docked preview beside the list (triage-style); Enter or double-click opens the full page.

variants.label: Links as graph
variants.summary: Links render as a graph: the question sidebar shows a local graph of its links, and the Links view opens on the workspace graph.

changes: Added a real Personal workspace with a single first-run screen (one primary action, agent status inline, four key hints); in round 1 the switcher only showed a toast.
Add link is now a working picker (link type + search, L); in round 1 its menu items did nothing.
File in outline lets you pick a Chapter 3 section and highlights the new line in the note; round 1 appended to the end of the note with no placement choice.
Search matches answer and recap text with a snippet ("11.8 TWh" finds CAISO); round 1 matched titles only.
Graph regrouped into project regions with labels below nodes, legend chips that filter link types, and select-then-open; round 1 was a tangled hub with clipped labels.
Standing passage hint under each answer names Highlight / Ask sub-question / File in note with keys; round 1 relied on selection or an unlabeled hover icon.
Replaced the Board-home variant (it duplicated Display → Board) with Project home, which tests an outline-first start.
Filter, Move to project, Archive (with Undo) and New project now work; agents recheck sign-in automatically while a question waits.
decisions: Is Ready vs Reviewed a useful distinction, or should a completed run simply be Done?
Do first-time users pick Follow-up vs Sub-question correctly from the composer switch?
Does 'Link' read as a connection between items, or do people expect saved URLs there (those are Notes here)?
Should home be the question list (A) or the project outline (B) for someone writing a thesis?
Is filing into a specific outline section worth the extra menu step compared with a single Clippings note?
